rows: Cold air met me at the door.

model.title: Redraft: 'The market was closing, the people were leaving and it was getting dark and the stalls were empty.'

parts.text: Replace 'people were leaving' with a precise image

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The market was closing. Stallholders folded their awnings like tired wings, and the light drained from the square. One lantern swung on its hook. Then that, too, went out.

keywords.def: improve a draft by changing words and sentences
rewrite a section to improve it
a small change that gains marks

questions.q: Five-minute routine on the practice draft (pupil PDF).
questions.a: Edits marked: splices fixed, two verbs swapped, apostrophes corrected, a paragraph break added.

questions.q: Name the three highest-value edits you made.
questions.a: Three edits with the mark they protect.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, redraft the middle paragraph of your description or story (from Weeks 1 to 3) to reach the next level on the success ladder. Starter: paste the paragraph, then improve it.
questions.a: A redraft with precise verbs, varied sentences, no splices and a stronger final line.

questions.q: Extend: explain which level your paragraph now reaches and why.
questions.a: A level with evidence from the ladder.

questions.q: Stretch: redraft the ending as well.
Which edit gains most in five minutes?
questions.a: A) Fixing three comma splices. Fixing splices raises AO5 at once; the others gain nothing.

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Run the five-minute routine: splices, apostrophes, verbs, first and last lines.
